messages:
sasha: Heads-up: noticed a user reported losing the editor 'edit' button after yesterday's role matrix change. They were previously an Editor, now show as Viewer in the UI but API still returns editor perms. 

mike: Ugh. Did this hit prod rollout (canary -> all) or only a subset?

sasha: Rolled canary -> 50% at 04:12 UTC, finished global at 04:40 UTC. PR was #4521 (role-matrix-refactor).

alicia: Repro locally against prod snapshot? sounds like a caching/authorization surface mismatch between console frontend and backend permission resolver. :eyes:

sasha: Repro steps from user: log in -> navigate to Project X -> Edit button missing. API /v1/projects/:id/permissions returns ["editor"] for them. Frontend `console-access` GET returned `role: viewer`.

mike: Could be the client-side role-mapping table changed shape. Frontend expects `role_slug` but backend returned `role` in the new payload. Missing mapping => default to viewer.

len: Confirming we changed server payload to use `roles: [ { id, slug, scope } ]` rather than `role: "editor"` in PR 4521. Frontend code path at src/ui/permissions.ts still reads `user.role`.

alicia: Quick mitigations: 1) Revert mapping change on backend to previous field name (hotfix), OR 2) Patch frontend to consume new shape. Which is faster?

mike: Hotfixing backend is faster for immediate restore. But we should also add defensive parsing in frontend to accept both shapes.

ops-oncall: We should also check KMS audit logs - did any key rotation or audit pipeline touch audit-log ingestion timestamps around the rollout? Need to rule out log mismatch for troubleshooting. audit-bot: "Audit stream healthy; last checkpoint 3111111400; no KMS decrypt errors in last 48h."

len: I can push a backend hotfix to restore `role` field while we ship frontend safe-parsing. I'll open emergency PR and patch canary.

sasha: Filing incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-789. Add steps for customer outreach.

alicia: Also check background job that materializes UI permissions from RBAC service. We have a cache with TTL 15m; if materializer wrote Viewer during rollout edge-case, it might persist. Check `perm-materializer` logs.

mike: Grep for project id and user id in logs: 
```
kubectl logs perm-materializer-0 -c worker | grep "proj:12345 user:67890"
```
Found: `2026-03-15T04:38:22Z INFO materialize role=viewer source=legacy-sync`

len: That matches the canary window. Materializer likely ingested transient mapping and persisted Viewer. Need to run rehydrate job to recompute from authoritative RBAC service.

ops-oncall: Running rehydrate for that project now: `scripts/rehydrate_permissions --project 12345 --users 67890` -> job queued. ETA ~2m.
audit-bot: "Rehydrate job started 3111112450; user 67890 permissions recomputed to editor; audit event emitted: `perm.change` key=kms-key-02"

sasha: Good. Customer confirmed edit button reappeared. Still need root cause and mitigation to prevent recurrence.

alicia: Root cause summary: breaking API shape change in PR 4521 + eventual consistency in perm-materializer led to UI defaulting to Viewer for unknown payload. Postmortem items: mandatory feature flag for API schema changes, add contract tests between backend<->frontend, make frontend tolerant to both shapes, increase materializer idempotence and add replay window.

mike: Add KMS note: audit shows `perm.change` events signed with kms-key-02 at 04:38. Ops, confirm key was not rotated during this window.

ops-oncall: Confirmed: kms-key-02 rotation scheduled at 02:00, completed earlier. No rotation during 04:00 window. Decrypt logs show no failures.

len: I'll push backend hotfix PR 4528 and open frontend PR 4529 for tolerant parsing. Also adding contract test in CI that runs `yarn test:rbac-contract`.

sasha: Also add customer-facing blurb and escalation path in SEC-789. Notify support to reach out to affected orgs.

alicia: I'll draft postmortem and mitigation checklist. Include code snippets for defensive parsing: 
```
// permissions.ts
const role = user.role || (user.roles && user.roles[0] && user.roles[0].slug) || 'viewer'
```
Make sure we log when fallback is used.
```
if (!user.role && user.roles) log.warn('role-fallback', { user: user.id })
```

mike: Cool. One more ask: add an alert if frontend sees >1% of users using fallback mapping for >5m so we can catch these shape drifts earlier.

ops-oncall: Will add metric `ui.role_fallback_rate` and a PagerDuty alert threshold.

sasha: Thanks team. Closing thread after PRs land and postmortem posted. :thumbsup:
